columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: Purpose-built for professional groups, networks, and communities, not casual consumer chat.
Supports unlimited groups and members; community size is not capped at higher tiers like some competitors.

Features: custom branding, professional member profiles, mobile-first UX, video rooms, Zapier/API integrations, analytics, moderation, and marketing support; free plan with discoverable profiles/groups.
Positioned vs Circle as a more professional, ad-free, GDPR-compliant alternative emphasizing quality and integrity.

strengths.title: Professional-grade, brandable communities
strengths.detail: Custom branding and professional profiles help orgs run credible, on-brand communities distinct from social networks.

strengths.title: Unlimited groups and members
strengths.detail: No member caps on higher tiers, fit for growing networks, associations, and industry communities.

strengths.title: Ad-free, mobile-first UX
strengths.detail: Clean UI without ads; designed to feel as easy as WhatsApp while staying business-appropriate.

strengths.title: Analytics, integrations, and support
strengths.detail: Built-in analytics, Zapier/API, and marketing support help owners measure engagement and connect Guild to their stack.

weaknesses.title: Niche focus on professional groups
weaknesses.detail: Less suited to broad consumer-social communities; product optimized around professional use cases.

weaknesses.title: Smaller ecosystem vs incumbents
weaknesses.detail: Fewer third-party tutorials, plugins, and templates than Slack, Facebook Groups, or Circle.

weaknesses.title: Limited built-in commerce/course tooling
weaknesses.detail: Does not match Circle’s deeper course and paywall features, monetization often routes through other tools.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Guild is real-time chat, groups, and community velocity. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Guild is a mobile-first community platform built for professional groups, networks, and communities, offering branded, ad-free spaces with profiles, messaging, and analytics.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Guild side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Guild you can use Community & Messaging as a first-class product job. The job is hanging out, announcements, and live conversation, not packaging knowledge into something strangers can browse later.

Using Kahana with Guild

You can use both. Guild keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep live conversation on Guild. Pin a Kahana hub or Club link in a channel, discuss live there, and assign the next ebook, video, or course from Kahana so the syllabus is not buried in the thread.
